title: Living under the sea
paragraphs: There are people living in almost every corner of our crowded planet. From the tops of mountains to deep underground, we’ve always been able to find habitable places to make a home. But with space at a premium, we’ve started to look even deeper for somewhere to live.

Throughout history, people have been fascinated by the idea of living underwater. More recently, the effects of human activity on the land have led some to look to the oceans for natural resources. Oceanographers and architects have looked at designing vessels, labs and underwater habitats to enable people to live and work in a submerged world. But, while dreams of an aquatic city have remained a fantasy, how close are we to making our home on the seabed a reality?

The pioneer of undersea living was Ian Koblick, sometimes described as an ‘aquanaut’. He claimed technology already existed to create underwater colonies supporting up to a hundred people. He even opened La Chalupa, once the largest and most advanced underwater habitat and research facility in the world.

A more recent and ambitious design for an underwater city is Ocean Spiral. Designed by the Japanese Shimizu Corporation, it’s a huge transparent globe attached to the seabed. It’s got a tower running through it to the surface, providing space for homes, offices and even an amusement park for five thousand residents. Masaki Takeuchi from the company told the BBC: “Our idea is to connect the sea surface and the deep sea vertically, and that way we believe that we can utilise the capability of the deep sea.”

Of course, there are engineering challenges in constructing an oceanic metropolis. And living underwater would have major effects on the human body, especially as there is an increase in atmospheric pressure which could lead to the bends. So, maybe it’s too soon to be packing our bags and setting up a new life three thousand metres under the sea!

vocabulary.entry: habitable /ˈhæbɪtəbl/ adj. 适宜居住的
vocabulary.example: The house is now habitable after being renovated.
vocabulary.translation: 这栋房子经过翻新后现在可以入住了。

vocabulary.entry: at a premium /æt ə ˈpriːmiəm/ 稀缺的；供不应求的
vocabulary.example: In the city centre, parking space is at a premium.
vocabulary.translation: 市中心的停车位十分紧缺。

vocabulary.entry: fascinate /ˈfæsɪneɪt/ v. 使着迷；使神魂颠倒
vocabulary.example: The mystery of the ancient ruins has always fascinated archaeologists.
vocabulary.translation: 古遗址的谜团一直让考古学家们着迷。

vocabulary.entry: underwater habitat /ˌʌndəˈwɔːtə ˈhæbɪtæt/ n. 水下栖息地
vocabulary.example: The scientists are testing a new type of underwater habitat in the Caribbean.
vocabulary.translation: 科学家们正在加勒比海测试一种新型水下栖息地。

vocabulary.entry: submerged /səbˈmɜːdʒd/ adj. 水下的；淹没的
vocabulary.example: The submerged city was discovered by a team of divers last year.
vocabulary.translation: 这座水下城市是去年由一支潜水队发现的。

vocabulary.entry: aquatic /əˈkwætɪk/ adj. 水栖的；水生的
vocabulary.example: The lake is home to a variety of aquatic plants and animals.
vocabulary.translation: 这片湖泊是多种水生动植物的栖息地。

vocabulary.entry: fantasy /ˈfæntəsi/ n. 幻想；空想
vocabulary.example: Her childhood fantasy was to become a fairy tale writer.
vocabulary.translation: 她儿时的梦想是成为一名童话作家。

vocabulary.entry: seabed /ˈsiːbed/ n. 海床；海底
vocabulary.example: The shipwreck lies on the seabed at a depth of 200 metres.
vocabulary.translation: 这艘沉船位于两百米深的海床上。

vocabulary.entry: pioneer /ˌpaɪəˈnɪə/ n. 先驱者；开拓者
vocabulary.example: She was a pioneer in the field of genetic engineering.
vocabulary.translation: 她是基因工程领域的先驱。

vocabulary.entry: aquanaut /ˈækwənɔːt/ n. 海底居民；水下工作者
vocabulary.example: The aquanaut spent two weeks living in the underwater research station.
vocabulary.translation: 这位水下工作者在水下研究站生活了两周。

vocabulary.entry: colony /ˈkɒləni/ n. 聚居地；群体
vocabulary.example: The scientists established a research colony in the remote desert.
vocabulary.translation: 科学家们在偏远沙漠建立了一个研究聚居地。

vocabulary.entry: facility /fəˈsɪləti/ n. 设施；设备
vocabulary.example: The sports centre has a wide range of facilities for members.
vocabulary.translation: 这座体育中心为会员提供种类繁多的设施。

vocabulary.entry: ambitious /æmˈbɪʃəs/ adj. 宏大的；有雄心的
vocabulary.example: The company has announced an ambitious plan to expand overseas.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司宣布了一项宏大的海外扩张计划。

vocabulary.entry: transparent /trænsˈpærənt/ adj. 透明的；清澈的
vocabulary.example: The window is made of a special transparent plastic.
vocabulary.translation: 这扇窗户是由一种特殊的透明塑料制成的。

vocabulary.entry: attach /əˈtætʃ/ v. 系上；固定
vocabulary.example: We need to attach the label to each piece of luggage.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要把标签贴在每件行李上。

vocabulary.entry: resident /ˈrezɪdənt/ n. 居民；住户
vocabulary.example: The residents of the town are protesting against the new road.
vocabulary.translation: 该镇居民正在抗议新建道路的计划。

vocabulary.entry: vertically /ˈvɜːtɪkli/ adv. 垂直地；直立地
vocabulary.example: The flagpole stands vertically in the middle of the square.
vocabulary.translation: 旗杆垂直矗立在广场中央。

vocabulary.entry: utilise /ˈjuːtəlaɪz/ v. 利用；使用
vocabulary.example: We need to utilise every available resource to solve the problem.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要利用一切可用资源来解决这个问题。

vocabulary.entry: engineering challenge /ˌendʒɪˈnɪərɪŋ ˈtʃælɪndʒ/ n. 工程难题
vocabulary.example: Building the bridge in the earthquake zone was a major engineering challenge.
vocabulary.translation: 在地震带建造这座桥梁是一项重大工程难题。

vocabulary.entry: atmospheric pressure /ˌætməsˈferɪk ˈpreʃə/ n. 气压
vocabulary.example: Changes in atmospheric pressure often affect the weather.
vocabulary.translation: 气压的变化往往会影响天气。

vocabulary.entry: the bends /ðə bendz/ n. 减压病
vocabulary.example: Divers must surface slowly to avoid getting the bends.
vocabulary.translation: 潜水员必须缓慢上浮，以防患上减压病。

vocabulary.entry: metropolis /məˈtrɒpəlɪs/ n. 大都市；首府
vocabulary.example: New York is a bustling metropolis on the east coast of America.
vocabulary.translation: 纽约是美国东海岸一座繁华的大都市。

sentences.english: There are people living in almost every corner of our crowded planet.
sentences.chinese: 在我们这个拥挤的星球上，几乎每个角落都有人居住。

sentences.english: From the tops of mountains to deep underground, we’ve always been able to find habitable places to make a home.
sentences.chinese: 从高山之巅到地下深处，人类总能找到适宜居住的地方安家落户。

sentences.english: But with space at a premium, we’ve started to look even deeper for somewhere to live.
sentences.chinese: 但随着空间愈发稀缺，我们开始将目光投向更深的地方，寻找新的栖身之所。

sentences.english: Throughout history, people have been fascinated by the idea of living underwater.
sentences.chinese: 自古以来，人类就对水下居住的构想十分着迷。

sentences.english: More recently, the effects of human activity on the land have led some to look to the oceans for natural resources.
sentences.chinese: 近年来，人类活动对陆地造成的影响，让一些人开始将目光投向海洋，挖掘其中的自然资源。

sentences.english: Oceanographers and architects have looked at designing vessels, labs and underwater habitats to enable people to live and work in a submerged world.
sentences.chinese: 海洋学家和建筑师们着手设计潜水器、实验室以及水下栖息地，希望能让人们在水下世界生活和工作。

sentences.english: But, while dreams of an aquatic city have remained a fantasy, how close are we to making our home on the seabed a reality?
sentences.chinese: 不过，尽管水上城市的梦想至今仍停留在幻想阶段，但我们距离在海床安家落户的现实还有多远呢？

sentences.english: The pioneer of undersea living was Ian Koblick, sometimes described as an ‘aquanaut’.
sentences.chinese: 水下居住的先驱者是伊恩·科布利克，他有时也被称为“海底居民”。

sentences.english: He claimed technology already existed to create underwater colonies supporting up to a hundred people.
sentences.chinese: 他声称，现有的技术已经能够建造可容纳上百人的水下聚居地。

sentences.english: He even opened La Chalupa, once the largest and most advanced underwater habitat and research facility in the world.
sentences.chinese: 他还曾创办了“拉查鲁帕”水下基地，这里一度是全球规模最大、技术最先进的水下栖息地与研究设施。

sentences.english: A more recent and ambitious design for an underwater city is Ocean Spiral.
sentences.chinese: “海洋螺旋”是近年来一个更为宏大的水下城市设计方案。

sentences.english: Designed by the Japanese Shimizu Corporation, it’s a huge transparent globe attached to the seabed.
sentences.chinese: 这个方案由日本清水建设株式会社设计，主体是一个固定在海床上的巨大透明球体。

sentences.english: It’s got a tower running through it to the surface, providing space for homes, offices and even an amusement park for five thousand residents.
sentences.chinese: 球体内有一座贯穿上下、直达海面的塔楼，可为五千名居民提供住宅、办公区域，甚至还有一座游乐园。

sentences.english: Masaki Takeuchi from the company told the BBC: “Our idea is to connect the sea surface and the deep sea vertically, and that way we believe that we can utilise the capability of the deep sea.”
sentences.chinese: 该公司的竹内正树在接受BBC采访时表示：“我们的构想是将海面与深海垂直连接起来，我们相信通过这种方式，能够充分开发深海的潜在价值。”

sentences.english: Of course, there are engineering challenges in constructing an oceanic metropolis.
sentences.chinese: 当然，建造一座海洋大都市面临着诸多工程难题。

sentences.english: And living underwater would have major effects on the human body, especially as there is an increase in atmospheric pressure which could lead to the bends.
sentences.chinese: 而且水下生活也会对人体产生重大影响，尤其是水下气压的升高可能会导致潜水员患上减压病。

sentences.english: So, maybe it’s too soon to be packing our bags and setting up a new life three thousand metres under the sea!
sentences.chinese: 如此看来，现在就打包行李，去三千米深的海底开启新生活，或许还为时过早。
